messages.content: You are a research assistant. Answer the user's research question using ONLY the provided source materials. Be concise (a few sentences). For each key point, cite which provided source(s) support it. Use the sources to answer as much of the question as they adequately support; where they are insufficient, conflicting, or not credible, say so for those specific points rather than guessing or declining the whole answer.

Research question:
Could you provide information on recent developments in cloud-based train control systems for urban rail transit? I'm also interested in understanding the key technologies involved.

Provided sources:

[Source A]
Source: Chang, Nan, Ou, Zhang, "Architecture Design and Reliability Evaluation of a Novel
Software-Defined Train Control System", Urban Rail Transit, 2022, 8(1):45-55 — DOI 10.1007/s40864-022-00165-y
Accessible mirror (Springer full text gated): https://journal.hep.com.cn/urt/EN/10.1007/s40864-022-00165-y

"This paper presents a novel urban transit signaling system architecture, software-defined train
control (SDTC), which is based on cloud and high-speed wireless communication technology. The core
functions of the proposed SDTC, including the onboard controller, are implemented in the cloud
platform, with only sensors and input-output (IO) units remaining on the trackside and the train."
This makes "signaling as a service possible"; "the mean time between failures is improved by 39%".

Source: The Paper (thepaper.cn, government account) — 2024-03-25 — all rights reserved
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_26806190

On Train Autonomous Control System (TACS): it is "vehicle-centric, characterized by deep integration
of signaling and vehicle, based on 'train-to-train' communication, realizing the leap of trains from
'automatic operation' to 'autonomous operation'." Compared with CBTC, "the availability index is
improved by 2 orders of magnitude, and braking latency is shortened by more than 150 ms." It enables
"autonomous resource management, autonomous routing, autonomous protection, autonomous adjustment,
autonomous learning and automatic driving."

Source: CRRC Qingdao Sifang — 2025-07-30 — all rights reserved
URL: https://www.crrcgc.cc/sfgf/2025-07/30/article_2025073015294946015.html

The TACS metro train "adopts 'vehicle + train control' deep-integration technology, building a fusion
technical system of network fusion, hard-wire fusion, speed-measurement fusion, display fusion, and
control fusion"; it is characterized by "fewer wayside devices, unified format, incorporating onboard
signaling equipment into the overall vehicle design"; it is "the country's first TACS-based fully
automatic autonomous-operation train".

Source: Casco / CRSC "Xihe" digital urban-rail solution (via The Paper) — 2024-06-28 — all rights reserved
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_27905099

"Xihe" is "an iterative upgrade of the 'fully automatic operation 2.0 system for smart metro'", based
on an "open rail-transit digital base", building "two core platforms of intelligent operation-control
and intelligent operation-maintenance", using "deep integration of advanced technologies such as
multi-source ubiquitous sensing, trustworthy artificial intelligence, big data, and the Internet of Things".

Source: Global Market Insights, "Communication-Based Train Control Market" (Report ID GMI8206) — 2025-04 — all rights reserved
URL: https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/communication-based-train-control-market

"CBTC systems play a pivotal role in optimizing train operations by enabling continuous, real-time
communication between trains and centralized traffic control centers." Core functions are "Automatic
train protection (ATP), automatic train operation (ATO), and automatic train supervision (ATS)."
Next-generation directions include "AI-driven analytics, IoT-based monitoring, and cybersecurity
enhancements." The 2024 market was USD 2.4 billion, with a 2025-2034 CAGR of 8.1%.

Answer the research question, citing the provided source(s).
